    Non-Uniform Spatial Discretization & Expanding Grids in Electrochemical Simulations¶

    In electrochemical experiments—such as potential-step chronoamperometry, cyclic voltammetry, and ultramicroelectrode (UME) measurements—faradaic electron transfer occurs exclusively at the electrode–electrolyte interface ($x = x_{\min}$). Consequently, steep concentration gradients ($\partial c / \partial x$) are confined to a thin diffusion boundary layer adjacent to the electrode surface, whereas the outer bulk solution experiences almost zero concentration change ($\nabla^2 c \approx 0$).

    When discretizing the 1D diffusion equation on a uniform spatial grid (Uniform1DMesh), achieving accurate interfacial fluxes ($J = -D \left.\partial c / \partial x\right|_{x_{\min}}$) at early times or high scan rates requires a very small step size $\Delta x_0$, forcing hundreds or thousands of nodes across the entire domain $[x_{\min}, x_{\max}]$.

    Non-uniform and expanding meshes (softpotato.grid) solve this multi-scale challenge by clustering fine grid intervals ($\Delta x_0 \ll \delta$) near active boundaries and smoothly coarsening node spacing into the bulk solution:

    • 5–20× faster simulation runtimes and 80–90% fewer spatial nodes compared to uniform grids at equal or superior current accuracy.
    • Second-order spatial accuracy ($\mathcal{O}(\Delta x^2)$) preserved across both interior Laplacian stencils and 3-point one-sided boundary flux operators.
    • Seamless integration with DiffusionProblem, curvilinear geometries (PlanarGeometry, SphericalGeometry, CylindricalGeometry), and all Soft Potato numerical solvers (scipy_ivp, crank_nicolson, implicit, explicit).

    Tutorial Objectives¶

    In this tutorial, you will learn how to:

    1. Understand the mathematical formulations of Uniform1DMesh, GeometricExpandingMesh, and ExponentialMesh (exponential, tanh, and sinh mappings).
    2. Automatically size simulation domains to the characteristic diffusion layer thickness $\delta = \text{factor} \cdot \sqrt{D \, t_{\max}}$ using diffusion_layer_thickness and create_diffusion_mesh.
    3. Construct one-sided and two-sided symmetric meshes using the three parameterizations of GeometricExpandingMesh.
    4. Compare uniform vs. expanding grids in 1D planar Cottrell chronoamperometry, spherical microelectrode radial diffusion, and reversible cyclic voltammetry.
    5. Verify second-order spatial convergence ($\mathcal{O}(\Delta x^2)$), mass conservation under zero-flux Neumann boundaries, and computational speedup using softpotato.analytical.benchmark.

    1. Theoretical Foundations & Mesh Formulations¶

    1.1 Physics-Informed Domain Sizing¶

    For semi-infinite diffusion with diffusivity $D$ over duration $t_{\max}$, the characteristic penetration thickness is defined as:

    $$\delta = \text{factor} \cdot \sqrt{D \, t_{\max}}, \quad x_{\max} = x_{\min} + \delta$$

    At the default multiplier $\text{factor} = 6.0$, the complementary error function decays to $\operatorname{erfc}(6/2) \approx 2.2 \times 10^{-5}$, ensuring that outer boundary perturbations remain below $0.003\%$ of the bulk concentration.

    1.2 Geometrically Expanding Meshes (GeometricExpandingMesh)¶

    A geometrically expanding grid scales consecutive cell intervals by a constant expansion ratio $\gamma > 1$:

    $$\Delta x_j = \Delta x_0 \cdot \gamma^j \quad (j = 0, 1, \dots, N - 2), \quad x_{j+1} = x_j + \Delta x_j$$

    Summing the finite geometric series relates the total domain length $L = x_{\max} - x_{\min}$ to the initial boundary step $\Delta x_0$, node count $N$, and expansion ratio $\gamma$:

    $$L = \Delta x_0 \sum_{j=0}^{N-2} \gamma^j = \Delta x_0 \frac{\gamma^{N-1} - 1}{\gamma - 1}$$

    GeometricExpandingMesh allows you to specify any two of (n_points, gamma, dx_min) and automatically solves for the third:

    1. (n_points, gamma): Computes $\Delta x_0 = L (\gamma - 1) / (\gamma^{N-1} - 1)$ analytically.
    2. (dx_min, gamma): Determines the minimum integer node count $N$ required to span $L$.
    3. (n_points, dx_min): Solves numerically via Brent's root-finding algorithm (scipy.optimize.brentq) for $\gamma > 1$.

    1.3 Exponential & Conformal-Mapping Meshes (ExponentialMesh)¶

    ExponentialMesh maps uniform computational coordinates $\xi_j = j / (N - 1) \in [0, 1]$ to physical coordinates $x(\xi) \in [x_{\min}, x_{\max}]$ using a dimensionless stretching parameter $\beta > 0$:

    • Exponential stretching (mapping="exponential"): $$x(\xi) = x_{\min} + L \frac{\exp(\beta \xi) - 1}{\exp(\beta) - 1}$$
    • Hyperbolic tangent stretching (mapping="tanh" / ExponentialMesh.from_tanh): $$x(\xi) = x_{\min} + L \left(1 - \frac{\tanh(\beta (1 - \xi))}{\tanh(\beta)}\right)$$
    • Hyperbolic sine conformal stretching (mapping="sinh" / ExponentialMesh.from_sinh): $$x(\xi) = x_{\min} + L \frac{\sinh(\beta \xi)}{\sinh(\beta)}$$

    1.4 Non-Uniform Finite-Difference Stencils¶

    On an arbitrary non-uniform grid with backward step $h_- = r_i - r_{i-1}$ and forward step $h_+ = r_{i+1} - r_i$, Soft Potato's Geometry classes evaluate the radial Laplacian $\nabla^2 c = \frac{\partial^2 c}{\partial r^2} + \frac{p}{r}\frac{\partial c}{\partial r}$ using exact 3-point Taylor stencils:

    $$\left.\frac{\partial c}{\partial r}\right|_i \approx -\frac{h_+}{h_-(h_- + h_+)} c_{i-1} + \frac{h_+ - h_-}{h_- h_+} c_i + \frac{h_-}{h_+(h_- + h_+)} c_{i+1}$$

    $$\left.\frac{\partial^2 c}{\partial r^2}\right|_i \approx \frac{2}{h_-(h_- + h_+)} c_{i-1} - \frac{2}{h_- h_+} c_i + \frac{2}{h_+(h_- + h_+)} c_{i+1}$$

    At the electrode surface ($i = 0$, with $h_0 = r_1 - r_0$ and $h_1 = r_2 - r_1$), the interfacial flux $J = -D \left.\frac{\partial c}{\partial r}\right|_{r_0}$ is evaluated via the second-order 3-point one-sided stencil:

    $$\left.\frac{\partial c}{\partial r}\right|_0 \approx -\frac{2 h_0 + h_1}{h_0(h_0 + h_1)} c_0 + \frac{h_0 + h_1}{h_0 h_1} c_1 - \frac{h_0}{h_1(h_0 + h_1)} c_2$$

    2. Constructing and Inspecting 1D Meshes with softpotato.grid¶

    Let's start by sizing a 1D diffusion domain for a typical aqueous species ($D = 1.0 \times 10^{-9}\text{ m}^2/\text{s}$, $t_{\max} = 1.0\text{ s}$) and exploring the mesh constructors and parameterizations in softpotato.grid.

    import os

# Set writable matplotlib cache directory
os.environ.setdefault("MPLCONFIGDIR", "/tmp/matplotlib")

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from softpotato.analytical.benchmark import (
    compute_error_metrics,
    run_grid_efficiency_benchmark,
    run_mass_conservation_benchmark,
    verify_spatial_convergence,
)
from softpotato.analytical.kinetics import nernst_equilibrium_concentrations
from softpotato.analytical.microelectrodes import microsphere_limiting_current
from softpotato.analytical.step import (
    cottrell,
    cottrell_spherical,
    step_concentration_profile,
)
from softpotato.analytical.voltammetry import randles_sevcik
from softpotato.constants import FARADAY
from softpotato.geometry import SphericalGeometry
from softpotato.grid import (
    ExponentialMesh,
    GeometricExpandingMesh,
    Uniform1DMesh,
    create_diffusion_mesh,
    diffusion_layer_thickness,
)
from softpotato.solver import DiffusionProblem, DirichletBC, get_solver

# Characteristic diffusion layer thickness for D = 1e-9 m^2/s, t_max = 1.0 s
D = 1.0e-9  # m^2/s (1e-5 cm^2/s)
t_max = 1.0  # s
delta = diffusion_layer_thickness(D=D, t_max=t_max, factor=6.0)
print(f"Characteristic diffusion layer thickness δ = {delta * 1e6:.2f} µm\n")

# Three parameterizations of GeometricExpandingMesh on [0, delta]
geom_from_N_gamma = GeometricExpandingMesh(0.0, delta, n_points=51, gamma=1.08)
geom_from_dx_gamma = GeometricExpandingMesh(0.0, delta, dx_min=1.0e-6, gamma=1.08)
geom_from_N_dx = GeometricExpandingMesh(0.0, delta, n_points=51, dx_min=1.0e-6)

# Exponential & conformal meshes via create_diffusion_mesh and classmethods
mesh_uni = create_diffusion_mesh(D=D, t_max=t_max, kind="uniform", n_points=51)
mesh_exp = create_diffusion_mesh(
    D=D, t_max=t_max, kind="exponential", n_points=51, beta=3.5
)
mesh_tanh = ExponentialMesh.from_tanh(0.0, delta, n_points=51, beta=2.8)
mesh_sinh = ExponentialMesh.from_sinh(0.0, delta, n_points=51, beta=3.5)
mesh_2sided = GeometricExpandingMesh(
    0.0, 50e-6, n_points=41, gamma=1.08, two_sided=True
)

print(
    f"{'Mesh Description':<34} | {'N':>4} | {'dx_min (µm)':>12} | {'dx_max (µm)':>12} | {'dx_max/dx_min':>13}"
)
print("-" * 86)
for label, m in [
    ("Uniform1DMesh (N=51)", mesh_uni),
    ("Geometric (N=51, γ=1.08)", geom_from_N_gamma),
    ("Geometric (dx_min=1µm, γ=1.08)", geom_from_dx_gamma),
    (f"Geometric (N=51, dx_min=1µm -> γ={geom_from_N_dx.gamma:.3f})", geom_from_N_dx),
    ("Exponential (N=51, β=3.5, exp)", mesh_exp),
    ("Exponential (N=51, β=2.8, tanh)", mesh_tanh),
    ("Exponential (N=51, β=3.5, sinh)", mesh_sinh),
    ("Geometric Two-Sided (50µm gap)", mesh_2sided),
]:
    ratio = m.dx_max / m.dx_min
    print(
        f"{label:<34} | {m.n_points:>4d} | {m.dx_min * 1e6:>12.3f} | {m.dx_max * 1e6:>12.3f} | {ratio:>12.1f}x"
    )

    3. Visualizing Node Distributions, Interval Spacings, and Two-Sided Grids¶

    Notice in the table above that with just $N = 51$ nodes across $\delta = 189.74\ \mu\text{m}$, a uniform grid has a boundary step of $\Delta x = 3.795\ \mu\text{m}$, whereas GeometricExpandingMesh(N=51, gamma=1.08) achieves a boundary resolution of $\Delta x_0 = 0.331\ \mu\text{m}$—more than 11× finer at the electrode surface without adding a single extra node!

    Below we compare:

    1. Coordinate stretching curves $x(\xi) / \delta$ vs. normalized index $\xi = j / (N - 1)$.
    2. Local cell interval profiles $\Delta x_j$ as a function of distance from the electrode $x_j$.
    3. 1D spatial node rug plots comparing one-sided electrode clustering against two-sided symmetric clustering (two_sided=True) for thin-layer or SECM tip–substrate gaps.

    n_vis = 31
meshes_vis = {
    "Uniform": Uniform1DMesh(0.0, delta, n_points=n_vis),
    r"Geometric ($\gamma = 1.12$)": GeometricExpandingMesh(
        0.0, delta, n_points=n_vis, gamma=1.12
    ),
    r"Exponential ($\beta = 3.5$)": ExponentialMesh(
        0.0, delta, n_points=n_vis, beta=3.5, mapping="exponential"
    ),
    r"Hyperbolic tanh ($\beta = 2.8$)": ExponentialMesh.from_tanh(
        0.0, delta, n_points=n_vis, beta=2.8
    ),
    r"Hyperbolic sinh ($\beta = 3.5$)": ExponentialMesh.from_sinh(
        0.0, delta, n_points=n_vis, beta=3.5
    ),
}

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 4.8))
xi = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, n_vis)

# Panel (a): Coordinate transformation x(xi) / delta
ax = axes[0]
for label, m in meshes_vis.items():
    ax.plot(xi, m.nodes / delta, marker="o", ms=3.5, lw=1.8, label=label)
ax.set_title(r"(a) Coordinate Mapping $x(\xi) / \delta$")
ax.set_xlabel(r"Normalized Node Index $\xi = j / (N - 1)$")
ax.set_ylabel(r"Normalized Coordinate $x / \delta$")
ax.grid(True, linestyle=":", alpha=0.6)
ax.legend(fontsize=8.5, loc="upper left")

# Panel (b): Interval spacing dx_j vs x_j
ax = axes[1]
for label, m in meshes_vis.items():
    ax.semilogy(m.nodes[:-1] * 1e6, m.dx * 1e6, marker="s", ms=3.5, lw=1.8, label=label)
ax.set_title(r"(b) Local Interval Spacing $\Delta x_j$ vs. $x_j$")
ax.set_xlabel(r"Distance from Electrode $x_j$ ($\mu$m)")
ax.set_ylabel(r"Interval Step $\Delta x_j$ ($\mu$m, log scale)")
ax.grid(True, which="both", linestyle=":", alpha=0.6)
ax.legend(fontsize=8.5, loc="lower right")

# Panel (c): 1D node rug plot (Uniform vs One-Sided vs Two-Sided)
ax = axes[2]
rug_meshes = [
    ("Uniform ($N=31$)", Uniform1DMesh(0.0, delta, n_points=n_vis), "tab:blue"),
    (
        r"One-Sided Geometric ($\gamma=1.12$)",
        GeometricExpandingMesh(0.0, delta, n_points=n_vis, gamma=1.12),
        "tab:orange",
    ),
    (
        r"One-Sided Exponential ($\beta=3.5$)",
        ExponentialMesh(0.0, delta, n_points=n_vis, beta=3.5),
        "tab:green",
    ),
    (
        "Two-Sided Geometric (two_sided=True)",
        GeometricExpandingMesh(0.0, delta, n_points=n_vis, gamma=1.18, two_sided=True),
        "tab:red",
    ),
    (
        "Two-Sided Exponential (two_sided=True)",
        ExponentialMesh(0.0, delta, n_points=n_vis, beta=3.0, two_sided=True),
        "tab:purple",
    ),
]
for y_idx, (label, m, color) in enumerate(rug_meshes):
    y_vals = np.full(m.n_points, y_idx)
    ax.plot(m.nodes * 1e6, y_vals, "|", color=color, ms=14, mew=1.8)
    ax.plot([0, delta * 1e6], [y_idx, y_idx], "-", color=color, lw=0.8, alpha=0.4)

ax.set_yticks(range(len(rug_meshes)))
ax.set_yticklabels([item[0] for item in rug_meshes], fontsize=8.5)
ax.set_ylim(-0.6, len(rug_meshes) - 0.4)
ax.set_title(r"(c) Node Clustering Across Domain $[0, \delta]$")
ax.set_xlabel(r"Spatial Coordinate $x$ ($\mu$m)")
ax.grid(True, axis="x", linestyle=":", alpha=0.6)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

    4. Planar Cottrell Chronoamperometry: Resolving Early-Time Boundary Layers¶

    Consider a 1D planar potential-step chronoamperometry experiment ($\text{Ox} + e^- \to \text{Red}$) where the surface concentration is stepped instantaneously to $c(0, t) = 0$ at $t = 0$:

    • Diffusion coefficient: $D = 1.0 \times 10^{-9}\text{ m}^2/\text{s}$
    • Bulk concentration: $c^* = 1.0\text{ mol/m}^3$ ($1.0\text{ mM}$)
    • Electrode area: $A = 1.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2$ ($1.0\text{ cm}^2$)
    • Time span: $t \in [0, 1.0]\text{ s}$

    At very early times (e.g., $t = 0.015\text{ s}$), the diffusion layer is only $\sqrt{\pi D t} \approx 6.9\ \mu\text{m}$ thick. Let's compare four spatial discretizations solved with get_solver("scipy_ivp"):

    1. Coarse Uniform Grid (Uniform1DMesh, $N = 50$): $\Delta x = 3.87\ \mu\text{m}$ (only 1–2 grid intervals inside the early boundary layer!).
    2. Fine Uniform Grid (Uniform1DMesh, $N = 500$): $\Delta x = 0.380\ \mu\text{m}$.
    3. Compact Geometric Expanding Grid (GeometricExpandingMesh, $N = 50$, $\gamma = 1.08$): $\Delta x_0 = 0.360\ \mu\text{m}$.
    4. Compact Exponential Grid (ExponentialMesh, $N = 50$, $\beta = 4.0$): $\Delta x_0 = 0.296\ \mu\text{m}$.

    5. Spherical Microelectrode Chronoamperometry on Expanding Radial Meshes¶

    At a spherical microelectrode of radius $r_0$, radial diffusion occurs over $r \in [r_0, r_0 + \delta]$:

    $$\frac{\partial c}{\partial t} = D \left( \frac{\partial^2 c}{\partial r^2} + \frac{2}{r} \frac{\partial c}{\partial r} \right)$$

    Because the geometric divergence term $\frac{2}{r}\frac{\partial c}{\partial r}$ is largest directly at the microelectrode surface ($r = r_0$), resolving the interfacial gradient with an expanding mesh (GeometricExpandingMesh.from_diffusion_layer(..., x_min=r0)) is crucial for capturing both the short-time Cottrell decay and the long-time spherical steady-state limiting current:

    $$I(t) = n F A D c^* \left( \frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi D t}} + \frac{1}{r_0} \right), \quad I_{\mathrm{ss}} = 4 \pi n F D c^* r_0$$

    In [4]:
    Copied!

    6. Reversible Cyclic Voltammetry on Geometrically Expanding Grids¶

    In Cyclic Voltammetry (CV), the electrode potential $E(t)$ sweeps linearly between $E_{\text{start}}$ and $E_{\text{vertex}}$ at scan rate $v$, continuously inverting the concentration gradient at the electrode surface. Under reversible Nernstian kinetics ($\text{Ox} + n e^- \rightleftharpoons \text{Red}$ with equal diffusivities $D_{\text{Ox}} = D_{\text{Red}} = D$), the surface concentrations follow:

    $$\frac{c_{\text{Ox}}(0, t)}{c_{\text{Red}}(0, t)} = \exp\left(\frac{n F (E(t) - E^{0\prime})}{R T}\right), \quad c_{\text{Ox}}(0, t) + c_{\text{Red}}(0, t) = c^*$$

    Let's simulate a reversible CV scan ($v = 0.1\text{ V/s}$) using GeometricExpandingMesh with only $N = 50$ nodes ($\gamma = 1.08$) and compare it against a coarse uniform mesh ($N = 50$), a fine uniform reference mesh ($N = 400$), and the analytical Randles–Ševčík peak current $I_p$.

    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    E_start = 0.35  # V
E_vertex = -0.35  # V
E0 = 0.0  # V
v_scan = 0.10  # V/s
t_switch = abs(E_start - E_vertex) / v_scan
t_cv_end = 2.0 * t_switch
t_cv_eval = np.linspace(0.0, t_cv_end, 400)


def cv_potential(t: float) -> float:
    if t <= t_switch:
        return E_start - v_scan * t
    return E_vertex + v_scan * (t - t_switch)


def c_ox_surface(t: float) -> float:
    c_ox, _ = nernst_equilibrium_concentrations(
        E=cv_potential(t), E0=E0, c_total=c_bulk, n=n_elec
    )
    return float(c_ox)


def c_red_surface(t: float) -> float:
    _, c_red = nernst_equilibrium_concentrations(
        E=cv_potential(t), E0=E0, c_total=c_bulk, n=n_elec
    )
    return float(c_red)


cv_meshes = {
    "Uniform (N=50)": Uniform1DMesh.from_diffusion_layer(
        D=D, t_max=t_cv_end, n_points=50
    ),
    "Uniform (N=400)": Uniform1DMesh.from_diffusion_layer(
        D=D, t_max=t_cv_end, n_points=400
    ),
    "Geometric (N=50, γ=1.08)": GeometricExpandingMesh.from_diffusion_layer(
        D=D, t_max=t_cv_end, n_points=50, gamma=1.08
    ),
}

cv_results = {}
for label, mesh in cv_meshes.items():
    prob_cv = DiffusionProblem(
        grid=mesh,
        diffusivity={"Ox": D, "Red": D},
        boundary_conditions={
            "Ox": (DirichletBC(c_ox_surface), DirichletBC(c_bulk)),
            "Red": (DirichletBC(c_red_surface), DirichletBC(0.0)),
        },
        initial_conditions={"Ox": c_bulk, "Red": 0.0},
        geometry="planar",
        n_electrons=n_elec,
    )
    cv_results[label] = solver_ivp.solve(
        prob_cv, t_span=(0.0, t_cv_end), t_eval=t_cv_eval
    )

ip_randles = float(
    randles_sevcik(
        v=v_scan, c_bulk=c_bulk, D=D, area=area, n=n_elec, scan_direction="cathodic"
    )
)
E_sweep = np.array([cv_potential(t) for t in t_cv_eval])

print(f"Analytical Randles–Ševčík I_pc = {ip_randles * 1e6:.3f} µA\n")
print(
    f"{'CV Grid Configuration':<28} | {'I_pc (µA)':>10} | {'|Err vs RS|':>12} | {'ΔEp (mV)':>10}"
)
print("-" * 68)
for label, sol in cv_results.items():
    curr = n_elec * FARADAY * area * sol.fluxes["Ox"]
    idx_pc = int(np.argmin(curr))
    idx_pa = int(np.argmax(curr))
    ipc = curr[idx_pc]
    delta_ep = (E_sweep[idx_pa] - E_sweep[idx_pc]) * 1e3
    err_rs = abs(ipc - ip_randles) / abs(ip_randles) * 100.0
    print(f"{label:<28} | {ipc * 1e6:>10.3f} | {err_rs:>11.3f}% | {delta_ep:>10.1f}")

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5.0))

# Panel (a): Cyclic Voltammogram
ax = axes[0]
for label, color, ls in [
    ("Uniform (N=400)", "black", "-"),
    ("Geometric (N=50, γ=1.08)", "tab:blue", "--"),
    ("Uniform (N=50)", "tab:red", ":"),
]:
    sol = cv_results[label]
    curr = n_elec * FARADAY * area * sol.fluxes["Ox"] * 1e6
    ax.plot(E_sweep, curr, linestyle=ls, color=color, lw=2.0, label=label)

ax.axhline(
    ip_randles * 1e6,
    color="gray",
    linestyle="-.",
    lw=1.2,
    label="Randles–Ševčík $I_{pc}$",

ax.legend(fontsize=8.0, loc="center right")

    E_start = 0.35 # V E_vertex = -0.35 # V E0 = 0.0 # V v_scan = 0.10 # V/s t_switch = abs(E_start - E_vertex) / v_scan t_cv_end = 2.0 * t_switch t_cv_eval = np.linspace(0.0, t_cv_end, 400) def cv_potential(t: float) -> float: if t <= t_switch: return E_start - v_scan * t return E_vertex + v_scan * (t - t_switch) def c_ox_surface(t: float) -> float: c_ox, _ = nernst_equilibrium_concentrations( E=cv_potential(t), E0=E0, c_total=c_bulk, n=n_elec ) return float(c_ox) def c_red_surface(t: float) -> float: _, c_red = nernst_equilibrium_concentrations( E=cv_potential(t), E0=E0, c_total=c_bulk, n=n_elec ) return float(c_red) cv_meshes = { "Uniform (N=50)": Uniform1DMesh.from_diffusion_layer( D=D, t_max=t_cv_end, n_points=50 ), "Uniform (N=400)": Uniform1DMesh.from_diffusion_layer( D=D, t_max=t_cv_end, n_points=400 ), "Geometric (N=50, γ=1.08)": GeometricExpandingMesh.from_diffusion_layer( D=D, t_max=t_cv_end, n_points=50, gamma=1.08 ), } cv_results = {} for label, mesh in cv_meshes.items(): prob_cv = DiffusionProblem( grid=mesh, diffusivity={"Ox": D, "Red": D}, boundary_conditions={ "Ox": (DirichletBC(c_ox_surface), DirichletBC(c_bulk)), "Red": (DirichletBC(c_red_surface), DirichletBC(0.0)), }, initial_conditions={"Ox": c_bulk, "Red": 0.0}, geometry="planar", n_electrons=n_elec, ) cv_results[label] = solver_ivp.solve( prob_cv, t_span=(0.0, t_cv_end), t_eval=t_cv_eval ) ip_randles = float( randles_sevcik( v=v_scan, c_bulk=c_bulk, D=D, area=area, n=n_elec, scan_direction="cathodic" ) ) E_sweep = np.array([cv_potential(t) for t in t_cv_eval]) print(f"Analytical Randles–Ševčík I_pc = {ip_randles * 1e6:.3f} µA\n") print( f"{'CV Grid Configuration':<28} | {'I_pc (µA)':>10} | {'|Err vs RS|':>12} | {'ΔEp (mV)':>10}" ) print("-" * 68) for label, sol in cv_results.items(): curr = n_elec * FARADAY * area * sol.fluxes["Ox"] idx_pc = int(np.argmin(curr)) idx_pa = int(np.argmax(curr)) ipc = curr[idx_pc] delta_ep = (E_sweep[idx_pa] - E_sweep[idx_pc]) * 1e3 err_rs = abs(ipc - ip_randles) / abs(ip_randles) * 100.0 print(f"{label:<28} | {ipc * 1e6:>10.3f} | {err_rs:>11.3f}% | {delta_ep:>10.1f}") fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5.0)) # Panel (a): Cyclic Voltammogram ax = axes[0] for label, color, ls in [ ("Uniform (N=400)", "black", "-"), ("Geometric (N=50, γ=1.08)", "tab:blue", "--"), ("Uniform (N=50)", "tab:red", ":"), ]: sol = cv_results[label] curr = n_elec * FARADAY * area * sol.fluxes["Ox"] * 1e6 ax.plot(E_sweep, curr, linestyle=ls, color=color, lw=2.0, label=label) ax.axhline( ip_randles * 1e6, color="gray", linestyle="-.", lw=1.2, label="Randles–Ševčík $I_{pc}$", ) ax.set_title(r"(a) Reversible Cyclic Voltammogram ($v = 100$ mV/s)") ax.set_xlabel(r"Potential $E - E^{0\prime}$ (V)") ax.set_ylabel(r"Current $I$ ($\mu$A)") ax.grid(True, linestyle=":", alpha=0.6) ax.legend(fontsize=8.5) # Panel (b): Concentration profiles at the cathodic peak ax = axes[1] idx_peak = int(np.argmin(cv_results["Geometric (N=50, γ=1.08)"].fluxes["Ox"])) sol_fine = cv_results["Uniform (N=400)"] sol_geom = cv_results["Geometric (N=50, γ=1.08)"] sol_coarse = cv_results["Uniform (N=50)"] ax.plot( sol_fine.x * 1e6, sol_fine["Ox"][idx_peak], "k-", lw=2.0, label=r"$c_{\mathrm{Ox}}$ Fine Uniform ($N=400$)", ) ax.plot( sol_fine.x * 1e6, sol_fine["Red"][idx_peak], "k--", lw=2.0, label=r"$c_{\mathrm{Red}}$ Fine Uniform ($N=400$)", ) ax.plot( sol_geom.x * 1e6, sol_geom["Ox"][idx_peak], "s", color="tab:blue", ms=4.5, label=r"$c_{\mathrm{Ox}}$ Geometric ($N=50$)", ) ax.plot( sol_geom.x * 1e6, sol_geom["Red"][idx_peak], "^", color="tab:cyan", ms=4.5, label=r"$c_{\mathrm{Red}}$ Geometric ($N=50$)", ) ax.plot( sol_coarse.x * 1e6, sol_coarse["Ox"][idx_peak], "o", color="tab:red", ms=5.0, fillstyle="none", label=r"$c_{\mathrm{Ox}}$ Coarse Uniform ($N=50$)", ) ax.set_xlim(0, 600) ax.set_title( f"(b) Peak Concentration Profiles ($E = {E_sweep[idx_peak] * 1e3:.0f}$ mV)" ) ax.set_xlabel(r"Distance from Electrode $x$ ($\mu$m)") ax.set_ylabel(r"Concentration $c(x, t) / c^*$") ax.grid(True, linestyle=":", alpha=0.6) ax.legend(fontsize=8.0, loc="center right") plt.tight_layout() plt.show()

    7. Spatial Order-of-Convergence ($\mathcal{O}(\Delta x^2)$) & Performance Benchmarking¶

    Soft Potato's softpotato.analytical.benchmark module provides automated verification routines for non-uniform grids:

    1. verify_spatial_convergence: Refines a grid family across $N \in (21, 41, 81, 161)$ keeping the total expansion ratio $\Delta x_{\max} / \Delta x_{\min}$ or stretching factor $\beta$ fixed, and performs log–log regression of the $L_\infty$ error against $\Delta x_{\text{eff}} = L / (N - 1)$ to verify second-order accuracy ($p \approx 2.0$).
    2. run_grid_efficiency_benchmark: Quantifies runtime speedup, memory scaling, and error norms comparing compact expanding meshes against uniform grids of increasing size.
    3. run_mass_conservation_benchmark: Verifies that total integrated species mass $\int c(x, t)\, dV$ is conserved under zero-flux NeumannBC(0.0) boundaries on non-uniform grids.
    In [6]:

    8. Summary & Practical Mesh Selection Guidelines¶

    Mesh Class / Factory Spacing Law Recommended Parameters Best Suited For
    Uniform1DMesh $\Delta x_j = \Delta x$ $N = 100\text{--}500$ Smooth initial profiles, Fourier benchmarks, or full-domain bulk reactions.
    GeometricExpandingMesh $\Delta x_j = \Delta x_0 \gamma^j$ $N = 50\text{--}100$, $\gamma = 1.04\text{--}1.10$ General-purpose chronoamperometry, cyclic voltammetry, and microelectrode radial diffusion.
    ExponentialMesh ("exponential") $x(\xi) \propto \dfrac{e^{\beta \xi} - 1}{e^\beta - 1}$ $N = 50\text{--}100$, $\beta = 3.0\text{--}4.5$ Smooth coordinate transformations and high-order Method of Lines (scipy_ivp) integration.
    ExponentialMesh.from_tanh $x(\xi) \propto 1 - \dfrac{\tanh(\beta(1-\xi))}{\tanh\beta}$ $N = 50\text{--}100$, $\beta = 2.0\text{--}3.5$ Boundary-layer clustering with gentle outer-domain spacing variation.
    ExponentialMesh.from_sinh $x(\xi) \propto \dfrac{\sinh(\beta \xi)}{\sinh\beta}$ $N = 50\text{--}100$, $\beta = 2.5\text{--}4.0$ Conformal coordinate stretching for steep interfacial concentration gradients.
    two_sided=True Symmetric from $x_{\min}$ & $x_{\max}$ $N = 61\text{--}121$, $\gamma = 1.05\text{--}1.08$ Thin-layer cells, SECM tip–substrate feedback gaps, and dual-electrode (electrodes="both") problems.

    Key Takeaways¶

    1. Use create_diffusion_mesh(D=..., t_max=...) for automatic domain sizing: It sets $x_{\max} = x_{\min} + 6\sqrt{D t_{\max}}$ automatically so outer boundary reflections never contaminate semi-infinite simulations.
    2. Moderate expansion factors ($\gamma \in [1.04, 1.10]$ or $\beta \in [3.0, 4.5]$) are optimal: They provide more than an order-of-magnitude finer resolution at the electrode surface ($x = x_{\min}$) while keeping consecutive step ratios smooth enough to preserve full $\mathcal{O}(\Delta x^2)$ finite-difference convergence.
    3. Full solver and geometry interoperability: Every Mesh1D subclass works as a drop-in replacement for np.linspace in DiffusionProblem across planar, spherical, and cylindrical geometries.
